## Purpose and entry points
Centrifugo is a Go real-time PUB/SUB server: application backends publish or manage subscriptions through HTTP/gRPC APIs; connected clients receive channel traffic over WebSocket, HTTP streaming, SSE, gRPC, or experimental WebTransport. Process startup is `main.go`, with CLI command wiring in `internal/app/cmd.go` and server lifecycle assembly in `internal/app/run.go`.

## Bootstrap, configuration, and server composition
The `serve` command loads, migrates, and validates configuration, then constructs shared dependencies and listeners. `internal/app/engine.go` owns the central real-time engine integration; `internal/app/mux.go` composes HTTP routes/transports; `internal/app/grpc.go` configures gRPC; `internal/config/config.go` and `internal/config/validate.go` define the configuration boundary. TLS, origins, logging, telemetry, brokers, and optional services are configured before serving.

## Client connection and transport boundary
Client traffic enters transport-specific adapters which normalize it into common connection/session behavior. Bidirectional WebSocket is implemented under `internal/websocket/`; unidirectional HTTP-streaming, SSE, gRPC, and WebTransport adapters are respectively `internal/unihttpstream/transport.go`, `internal/unisse/transport.go`, `internal/unigrpc/transport.go`, and `internal/wt/transport.go`. `internal/client/client.go` and `internal/client/handler.go` implement client protocol handling, subscriptions, commands, and message delivery.

## Authentication and request policy
HTTP/client requests pass middleware for protocol enforcement, observability, connection limiting, CORS, and auth. Core paths include `internal/middleware/auth.go`, `internal/middleware/auththrottle.go`, and `internal/middleware/otel.go`. JWT validation supports signing keys/JWKS through `internal/jwtverify/token_verifier_jwt.go` and `internal/jwks/manager.go`; proxy/origin integration is represented by `internal/app/proxy.go` and `internal/origin/origin.go`. This boundary separates untrusted client credentials and backend authorization decisions from the messaging engine.

## Backend API and proxy operations
Backends call generated HTTP and gRPC APIs to publish, inspect connections, refresh credentials/subscriptions, and issue RPC-related operations. Public API dispatch is in `internal/api/api.go`, `internal/api/handler.go`, and `internal/api/grpc.go`; wire contracts are generated from `internal/apiproto/api.proto`. `internal/proxy/` implements outbound calls to an application backend for connect, subscribe, publish, refresh, and RPC hooks, with HTTP and gRPC variants.

## Distribution, persistence, and ingestion
The engine scales publications, presence, history, and cross-node control via pluggable brokers. Redis/NATS options are under `internal/redisnatsbroker/broker.go`, `internal/natsbroker/broker.go`, and `internal/pubsub/`; PostgreSQL-backed map and stream brokers are `internal/pgmapbroker/pgmapbroker.go` and `internal/pgstreambroker/pgstreambroker.go`. External event ingestion supports Kafka, PostgreSQL, Redis Streams, NATS JetStream, AWS SQS, Google Pub/Sub, and Azure Service Bus in `internal/consuming/`. PostgreSQL outbox workers in `internal/pgoutbox/` support transactional-outbox/CDC delivery.

## Operations and observability
The service exposes health and runtime operations through `internal/health/health.go` and embedded admin handling in `internal/admin/handlers.go`. Metrics are centralized in `internal/metrics/metrics.go`, with optional Graphite export at `internal/metrics/graphite/graphite.go`; OpenTelemetry provider setup is `internal/telemetry/provider.go`. Deployment targets include a container image (`Dockerfile`), local dependency composition (`docker-compose.yml`), and release packaging (`.goreleaser.yml`).
